in_english.name: Sauban
in_english.long_meaning: Sauban is an Arabic name meaning 'freed slave' or 'loyal servant'. It originates from the Arabic root 's-w-b' which connotes the idea of liberation or being set free. The name holds significant historical and spiritual importance as it was the name of one of the companions of Prophet Muhammad, Sauban bin Bicde, who was known for his loyalty and piety.

data.cultural_impact: The name Sauban holds a significant cultural impact in certain Muslim communities, especially those that value strength, bravery, and leadership. Sauban is reminiscent of the powerful and majestic lion, an animal meticulously depicted in Islamic art and symbolism. The regal and brave nature of the lion resonates with many Muslims, representing the ideal character for those in positions of power and leadership.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, Sauban can also be seen as a symbol of faith and resilience. Just as the lion fearlessly faces their adversaries, those who bear the name Sauban are encouraged to face life's challenges with courage and unwavering faith. In Islamic tradition, the lion is said to be the guardian of paradise, symbolizing the idea that with faith and determination, one can overcome obstacles and reach a state of spiritual enlightenment. Ultimately, Sauban serves as a reminder to embrace the traits of strength, bravery, and unwavering faith in all aspects of life.

historical_references.reference: Sauban was a famous Sufi saint and scholar from Baghdad during the Abbasid Caliphate. He was known for his piety, knowledge of hadith, and his association with the influential Sufi scholar Al-Junayd.
historical_references.context: The Abbasid Caliphate was the dominant Islamic power during this time, ruling from Baghdad. Sufism, an Islamic mystical tradition, was developing in this period.

historical_references.reference: Sauban is also known as Sa'ban ibn al-Murr, and he is said to have been a companion of the Sufi master Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani in Baghdad during the late 11th to early 12th century AD.
historical_references.context: Abd al-Qadir al-Jilani was a prominent Sufi master and founder of the Qadiriyya Sufi order. Sauban is considered one of his most notable companions.
